node: DEM碎冰场直航冰阻力验证面成熟化: MT Uikku实冰实验锚对标 + Lindqvist解析交叉验证

decision.question: Can the plan-view floe DEM of this repository be promoted to a REAL (evidence-graded) broken-ice direct-navigation resistance model, validated against an analytic reference and against full-scale experiment?
alternatives: A: promote to REAL if C1..C7 all pass (DEM within 15% of Lindqvist at the standard case and within 20% of the MT Uikku anchor)
B: keep WITHHELD and publish a quantified gap plus the missing-mechanism budget (honest FAIL)
C: declare NOT_SUPPORTED for plan-view DEM in broken ice and specify the required 2.5D/3D extension
decision.decision_rule: A is adopted only if every criterion passes; otherwise the outcome is the strongest of {B, C} that the evidence supports, and C1 is reported as FAIL with its number.

hypothesis.H1: A 60%-concentration broken-ice field at V = 3 m/s and h = 1.0 m gives a DEM resistance within 15% of the level-ice Lindqvist anchor for the same ship and ice.
hypothesis.H1_rationale_for_scepticism: Lindqvist is an intact-sheet formula; broken ice is physically expected to sit BELOW it (the repository's own broken-ice closed form suppresses bending and adds momentum flux). H1 is therefore the strict version of the cross-check and is expected to be informative either way.
hypothesis.H2: R_ice increases monotonically with ship speed V in [2, 5] m/s (Pearson r > 0.95).
hypothesis.H3: R_ice increases monotonically with ice thickness h in [0.5, 1.5] m (Pearson r > 0.95).
hypothesis.H5: The DEM reproduces the MT Uikku full-scale broken-ice resistance within 20%.

outcome_metrics.primary: steady-window mean ice resistance R_ice [kN] (reaction of the floes on the hull along the track)
secondary: standard deviation, standard error and stationarity drift of R_ice over the steady window
friction share of the hull power (audit: R V = P_drag + P_friction)
mean hull-floe contact count and mean floe speed
realised field concentration and floe count (field reproducibility)

baseline_and_controls.analytic_baseline: tensordem.level_ice.formula.lindqvist_components for the same ship (MT Uikku transport hull), ice (MT Uikku sheet III material) and speed
baseline_and_controls.like_for_like_analytic: tensordem.ice_resistance_scaling.broken_ice_anchor (bending suppressed below the bending length, momentum flux added)
baseline_and_controls.negative_control: field-free case (one 5 cm floe parked outside the track) must give R = 0; a 10 % concentration field must stay below 25 % of the standard resistance
baseline_and_controls.numerical_controls: contact-law A/B (crushing-limited vs linear penalty), hull-form A/B (wedge bow vs block), floe-size A/B (3 m vs 8 m), time-step halving (dt = 2 ms vs 4 ms), three field seeds

stopping_rules.success: all of C1..C7 PASS -> evidence grade REAL for broken-ice direct-navigation resistance
stopping_rules.honest_fail: any criterion FAIL or WITHHELD -> criterion reported with its number; the evidence grade stays WITHHELD and the gap is quantified; no threshold is relaxed after seeing results
stopping_rules.no_tuning_rule: after the first standard-case number is seen, contact-law, hull-form, floe-size, friction and material parameters are frozen; the only permitted re-runs are the predeclared A/B, seed and dt variants
stopping_rules.abort: a case that exceeds 30 min wall time is reported with the steps it completed and marked incomplete

controlled: floe placement (seeded jittered lattice), floe radius distribution, field concentration
ship outline (length 105 m, beam 26 m, draught 8 m, entry angle 18 deg), speed, start position
ice material (MT Uikku sheet III compressive/flexural strength, modulus)
contact law parameters (friction 0.10, normal damping 0.2, chord regularisation 5 mm)
time step, integrator (velocity Verlet), record interval, steady window
confounders: the 2D plan-view formulation has no vertical (heave) coupling to the hull, so the hydrostatic submersion term of intact-ice resistance has no counterpart
the floe pack has free lateral boundaries (no pack pressure from an unbounded field)
floes are rigid disks: no fracture, no ride-up, no rubble pile
the DEM resistance is dominated by isolated impacts, so the relative statistical noise is large

repetitions.rationale: the standard case is averaged over three independent field realisations because the resistance of an open pack is impact dominated; sweep points use seed 7 only and report std/SEM so the trend test is judged against the measured scatter as well
repetitions.dt_convergence: standard case repeated at half the time step

environment.runtime: python 3.11, torch 2.7.1 CPU, float64, one thread per case, one process per case
environment.provenance: every case record carries the ledger SHA-256 of the parameter ledger and the material state

analysis_plan.steady_window: records with the ship fully embedded in the field (stem abaft the ship length and forward of the field end), restricted to the last half of the transit
analysis_plan.aggregation: arithmetic mean over the window; standard deviation and standard error reported; stationarity drift = (second half - first half) / mean
analysis_plan.trend_tests: Pearson correlation of R_ice against V and against h, plus an explicit monotonicity check
analysis_plan.outliers: no point is discarded; the peak resistance is reported next to the mean
analysis_plan.missing_data: C4 is WITHHELD because the repository ships no broken-ice experimental case - the gap is named, not filled with a level-ice number

interpretation_limits: a PASS of C1 would show magnitude agreement with a level-ice formula, not that the DEM is physically complete
the plan-view formulation cannot represent submersion, ride-up, fracture or rubble piling; a disagreement with Lindqvist is therefore expected to be a model-structure result, not a coefficient error
no broken-ice full-scale experiment is available in the repository, so absolute broken-ice accuracy stays WITHHELD regardless of the analytic cross-check
